title: Which even numbers lie between these two?
description: Tens and ones are split apart to check that zero, two, four, six and eight at the end make a number of twos. The same idea then lists the numbers that two divides between three hundred and ninety nine and four hundred and eleven, and Keeko's doubt about where the list starts is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: tens are whole twos, so only the last digit decides, and the list is found by going up from the first number with an even last digit. Watch for students who start counting in twos from the odd number.

source: Do you agree that numbers divisible by 2 end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8? List the multiples of 2 between 399 and 411.
video_script.why: The child checks the statement in both directions by splitting a number into tens and ones, and then lists the numbers between two given numbers by their last digits.
video_script.substitution: Split a number into tens and ones, and see which last digits leave nothing over after twos are taken out. Then go up from the first number that ends in an even digit.
video_script.anchor: a number strip from 399 to 411, with the numbers that end in an even digit lit
video_script.wrong_answer: the list starts at four hundred and one
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko starts counting in twos from three hundred and ninety nine and lands on four hundred and one. Three hundred and ninety nine is odd, so these jumps land on odd numbers only, and the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, we agree with the statement

final_answer.spoken: yes, we agree, and the numbers are four hundred, four hundred and two, four hundred and four, four hundred and six, four hundred and eight and four hundred and ten

maths_rules: 10 = 5 x 2, so every ten is a whole number of twos
the last digits 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 are 0 x 2, 1 x 2, 2 x 2, 3 x 2, 4 x 2, whole twos
so 2 divides a number exactly when its last digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8
399 ends in 9, so it is not on the list; 400 is the first number after it that ends in an even digit
the list: 400, 402, 404, 406, 408, 410; the next one, 412, is past 411
video_script.design: One idea: tens are whole twos, so the last digit decides, and the list starts at the first number with an even last digit. Assumes the earlier counts in twos. Wrong idea: start counting in twos from the odd number. The number strip stays on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a statement card: two divides a number exactly when it ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8; a number strip from 399 to 411 below it

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside the statement card
marks.list: the number strip from 399 to 411 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about numbers that two divides.
<bookmark mark='card'/>Here is a statement. Two divides a number exactly when it ends in zero, two, four, six or eight.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Do you agree?
<bookmark mark='list'/>Then list the multiples of two between three hundred and ninety nine and four hundred and eleven.

beats.on_screen: the statement card and the strip hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: jumps of 2 from zero land on 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and skip the numbers in between

marks.jump: jumps of two from zero land on 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10
marks.skip: the numbers in between are greyed out

narration: <bookmark mark='jump'/>Start at zero and jump in twos. The jumps land on two, four, six, eight and ten.
<bookmark mark='skip'/>The numbers in between are skipped.

beats.on_screen: Given: the statement about the last digit 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8; the limits 399 and 411

marks.given: the statement and the two limits are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the statement about the last digit.
The limits are three hundred and ninety nine, and four hundred and eleven.

beats.on_screen: To find: is the statement right in both directions; the list between 399 and 411

marks.find: the two questions are written in a list

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to check whether the statement is right in both directions, and then write the list.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, tens are whole twos: 10 = 5 x 2, so only the last digit decides

marks.ten: a number is split into tens and ones, and each ten is cut into five twos
marks.ones: the single ones are set apart and lit

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Step one, split a number into tens and ones.
Every ten is five twos, so the tens leave no gap.
<bookmark mark='ones'/>Only the last digit can leave a gap.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, all last digits: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 are whole twos; 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 leave 1 over

marks.even: the digits 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8 are ticked as whole twos
marks.odd: the digits 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 are marked with one left over

narration: <bookmark mark='even'/>Step two, look at every last digit.
Zero, two, four, six and eight are whole twos. They leave nothing over.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>One, three, five, seven and nine leave one over.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, the list: 399 ends in 9, so it is out; 400, 402, 404, 406, 408, 410; 412 is past 411

marks.start: 399 is crossed out because its last digit is 9
marks.first: 400 is lit as the first number that ends in an even digit
marks.end: 408 and 410 appear, and 412 is greyed out past the limit

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Step three, find the first number after three hundred and ninety nine.
Three hundred and ninety nine ends in nine, an odd digit.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Four hundred is the first number that ends in an even digit.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Then comes four hundred and two, four hundred and four, four hundred and six.
<bookmark mark='end'/>Then four hundred and eight, and four hundred and ten.
The next one, four hundred and twelve, is past the end.

marks.check: the five jumps from 400 to 410 are drawn and the six numbers are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the count.
From four hundred to four hundred and ten is ten.
Ten divided by two is five jumps, so there are six numbers.

marks.rest: the last three numbers of the list are lit

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Yes, we agree with the statement.
The numbers are four hundred, four hundred and two, four hundred and four.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Then four hundred and six, four hundred and eight, and four hundred and ten.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble; jumps of 2 from 399 land on 401, 403, 405 and the bubble is struck through; the jumps from 0 reach 400

marks.doubt: the bubble appears over the strip with jumps of two from 399
marks.odd: the jumps from 399 land on 401, 403 and 405, all odd
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the count from zero reaches 400

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the list starts at four hundred and one.
It jumps by two from three hundred and ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>But that jump starts from an odd number, so it lands only on odd numbers.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The count in twos starts at zero. Four hundred is the first number on it after three hundred and ninety nine.
